clue.text: An appearance — not in dock

parts.note: someone not in is out
to dock a tail is to crop it, cut it short

explanation.surface: A sighting of someone who is absent from the courtroom dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests a courtroom or harbour, but here it is the verb meaning to cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock that shows itself above the ground, an appearance at the surface.

clue.text: Orator's opening part of speech I would call too much

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: An orator starts a speech and declares it excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' is the bridge sense: to overbid is to bid more than the hand is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a bid is a call, and an overbid offers more than one can make.

clue.text: Rather as undergraduates work

definitions.meaning: students work towards a university qualification

explanation.surface: Students labour more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means somewhat, and read literally describes students working for a university award.

clue.text: Valued as an artist, Edward

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Ted is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward was highly regarded as a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rated has been assessed and esteemed, given a value.

clue.text: Girl with a name that's aristocratic

parts.note: Patricia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl whose name sounds noble.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrician was a member of Rome's noble class, so the word means of noble birth.

clue.text: Variety act incorporating simple entertainment

indicators.note: incorporating means taking another piece into the body of the first
variety suggests a mixed-up version, so the letters of act are shuffled

parts.note: simple, unadorned, means bare

explanation.surface: A music-hall turn that includes some plain amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' scrambles ACT into CAT, and 'incorporating' puts BARE inside it, after CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is a kind of nightclub show, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Stop searching

definitions.meaning: to ... something down is to stop it

explanation.definitionFit: To close is to end or shut down, and a close look is a thorough, probing one.

clue.text: Lover with mounting appeal — but not quite satisfied with good looks

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or lover

indicators.note: mounting means rising, so in a down answer the word reads upwards

parts.note: it is sex appeal

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: after a meal one is full, satisfied

explanation.surface: A suitor whose attraction grows, though he is not quite contented with handsome looks.
explanation.walkthrough: IT (sex appeal) is 'mounting', read upwards as TI; 'not quite' cuts FULL to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beautiful is attractive in appearance, lovely to look at.

clue.text: In Cairo, we really need a boatman

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Visitors to Cairo want someone to row them on the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Cairo, we really'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower is someone who propels a boat with oars, an oarsman.

clue.text: To be or not to, towards the end, it falls into place

indicators.note: falls into suggests the letters tumble into a new order
towards the end points to the closing words of the quotation

explanation.surface: Hamlet's soliloquy finally settles into its proper position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards the end' takes OR NOT TO from the quotation, and 'falls into' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is a city in Canada, a place.

clue.text: Former officer is after a raise

parts.note: ex- means former
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An ex-officer is angling for a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' looks like a noun, a pay rise, but it is the verb: to exalt is to raise up.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to elevate or lift them high, in rank or praise.

clue.text: Defective warrant for the arrest of Miss March about fighting

indicators.note: arresting someone holds them, so the shuffled letters enclose the other piece
something defective is faulty, so the letters of warrant are rearranged
about here means turned round, so the heroine's name reads backwards

parts.note: Jo March is the heroine of Little Women

explanation.surface: A flawed warrant is issued to arrest a woman over a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of WARRANT (from 'Defective') is TRANWAR; 'about' turns JO into OJ, and 'for the arrest of' holds it inside after TR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan War is the legendary conflict over Helen, a famous episode of combat.

clue.text: Reformed characters in Ireland live around subsistence level

indicators.note: around places the letters of Ireland about the other piece before shuffling

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ireland's characters, reformed, are living near the poverty line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' rearranges IRELAND with BE ('live') put 'around' into it; 'characters in' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The breadline is the minimal income on which people can barely survive.

clue.text: Go round one foreign city

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a go in a game is your turn
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Make a circuit of a single city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' reads as one phrase, but 'Go' is TURN and 'round' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a city in northern Italy, so foreign from a British view.

clue.text: Communist rejected by English city

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: A Communist is turned away by an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Derby is a city in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: What you might say, before the meal, to a duke

definitions.text: What you might say, before the meal, to a duke

parts.words: What you might say, before the meal, to a duke
parts.note: the formal address to a duke, read as an instruction to say the blessing before eating

explanation.surface: Words to a duke at the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is formally addressed with this phrase, which also reads as asking him to say the blessing.

clue.text: Settle change of topic about Latin thereby

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the other piece
a change of the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: a settle is a long wooden bench, a kind of sofa

explanation.surface: Resolve a switch of subject regarding Latin, as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges TOPIC into IPCTO, which goes 'about' SOFA. 'Settle' looks like a verb but is the noun, a high-backed bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipso facto is a Latin phrase meaning by that very fact, hence thereby.

clue.text: City's worried about catalogue of fashion

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the other piece
worried means agitated, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of city plus s
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: The City is anxious over a clothing brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns CITYS into STYIC, which goes 'about' LIST, after STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylistic means relating to style, the manner or fashion of something.

clue.text: Conservative rumour — one concerning the state

parts.note: a dit is a sailor's slang word for a yarn or rumour
I is the Roman numeral one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Gossip about a Tory, someone concerned with affairs of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks political here but means condition, as in good state.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing's condition is the state it is in.

clue.text: Hurts, they say, to measure this commonness

definitions.text: Hurts, they say, to measure this
definitions.meaning: hertz, which sounds like hurts, is the unit for measuring cycles per second
how often something happens, its rate of occurrence

explanation.surface: Pain is reported as a way to gauge how often something occurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hertz is the unit of frequency in physics, and frequency also means how common or often something is.

clue.text: It's important to turn boat's head up when taking in water amidships

indicators.note: taking in means the turned word holds the other piece
up means rising, so in a down answer the word reads upwards

parts.note: to luff is to steer a boat's head into the wind

indicators.note: amidships means the middle of the word, its centre letters

explanation.surface: Turning the bow is vital when a boat ships water in its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: LUFF read 'up' gives FFUL; 'amidships' takes ATE from the middle of 'water', and 'taking in' puts it inside after F.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fateful has momentous consequences, so it matters greatly.

clue.text: Moony girl going from one side to the other

parts.note: L is left, one side
Una is a girl's name
R is right, the other side

explanation.surface: A dreamy girl crossing from one side of the room to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: UNA goes from L (left) to R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Moony can mean of or like the moon, which is the sense of lunar.

clue.text: Money invested in animal that kills vermin — a fine specimen

indicators.note: invested in means put inside another word

parts.note: a ratter is a dog or cat that catches rats
L is the pound sign, money

explanation.surface: Funds are put into a pest-killing dog, a fine example of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rattler' is old British slang for something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, a rattler is a first-rate example of something, a corker.

clue.text: I have a suggestion about Welsh way of speaking

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a tang is a hint or trace, a suggestion of flavour

explanation.surface: Someone offers an idea about a Welsh accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have' only joins: TANG goes 'about' W.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a distinctive nasal accent, a regional manner of talking.

clue.text: It's hard standing in protective clothing

definitions.meaning: a paved area at an airport where aircraft stand
garment worn to keep clothes clean when cooking

explanation.definitionFit: An apron is both a paved area at an airfield and a garment tied over the front of clothes.

clue.text: Pelt with rock one who's too close

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's skin
flint is a hard rock

explanation.surface: Attack someone standing too near by throwing stones at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like the verb to throw at, but it is the noun, a hide. 'close' means stingy, not near.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is called close-fisted or close, mean with money.

clue.text: In a way, very little …

annotationWithheld.why: 'In a way, very little ...' gives ST around WEE, but its definition 'confectionery' sits in the clue to 24-down, so this clue as held has no defining word

clue.text: — confectionery is fake

explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft toffee-like sweet, and to fudge figures is to falsify them.

clue.text: Leaders in Falkland Island without a force prepared to fight. Heavens!

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters
without means leaving out a piece from the word

parts.note: an armament is a military force equipped for war
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation about the Falklands being undefended against an army ready for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops one A from ARMAMENT to leave RMAMENT. The exclamation mark dresses the definition as a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the sky, the vault of the heavens above.

clue.text: Routine — it can be boring

explanation.definitionFit: A drill is both a repeated training exercise and a tool that makes holes.

clue.text: Clement — name that's advanced all round

indicators.note: all round means the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: money advanced is lent
i.e. means that is

explanation.surface: Clement is a name that has been put forward on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clement' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning merciful. LENT goes 'all round' N and IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement and lenient both describe being merciful and mild in judgement.

clue.text: Gain about two points daily

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to clear a sum is to gain it as profit
N and E are two compass points

explanation.surface: Earn around a couple of points each day.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is British for a cleaning woman who comes in each day; it looks like an adverb here.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a daily is a domestic help who comes in to do housework.
